To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adding a permanent display to a communication board did not significantly alter the interactional patterns of nonspeaking persons with their speaking partners and (2) the addition of a permanent display did reduce the number of message reformulations and the number of turns related to reformulations in the interactions between nonspeakers and their speaking partners.

the addition of the electronic output display (a semipermanent, nonvolatile display) did not have the hypothesized effect of reducing the number of turns and reformulations, but did have the hypothesized effects of reducing the number and rate of reformulations.
the use of an EOD did not have a significant impact on any of the variables measured except the rate of message formulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interplay of communication output mode and interactional style between nonspeakers and their speaking partners, and with the effects of this interplay on the quality of the interactions and the efficiency of the communication.
the interplay between the output modes of communication devices and the interactional styles of persons using them.
the interplay of communication output mode and interactional style.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there was no significant change in the interaction of the two dyads due to the presence or absence of the EOD.
the addition of the EDD did not have a significant effect on any of the interactional variables measured in this study.
the use of the EOD did not significantly change any aspects of the interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of an EOD did not significantly alter the interactional dynamics of the dyads, and, in fact, the addition of an electronic device may have actually increased the rate of message formulation problems.
the use of an EOD does not appear to have a significant impact on the quality of the interaction between NSPs and SPs.
the addition of the EDD does not appear to affect interactional variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of a permanent display of information does not necessarily lead to more effective interactions between nonspeakers and their speaking partners.
the EOD is not a panacea for the communication difficulties faced by nonspeaking persons.
the use of EOD does not appear to have any effect on the interactional behavior of NSPs and their partners.
